# Security Rules

> **CRITICAL** — Claude must follow these rules at all times. Non-negotiable.

## Secrets & Credentials

- **NEVER** hardcode secrets, API keys, tokens, or passwords in code or comments.
- **NEVER** log sensitive data (tokens, passwords, PII, card numbers).
- **NEVER** commit `.env` files or secret files to version control.
- All secrets must come from environment variables or a secrets manager.

## Input Validation

- Validate and sanitise **all** user input at the boundary (controller / API handler).
- Use parameterised queries / prepared statements — never string-interpolated SQL.
- Validate file uploads: type, size, and sanitise filenames.
- Reject or strip unexpected fields (use allowlist-based validation).

## Authentication & Authorisation

- Always check authentication before authorisation.
- Authorisation must be checked **in the service layer**, not just the controller.
- Use short-lived tokens; implement refresh-token rotation.
- Passwords must be hashed with bcrypt / argon2 — never MD5 or SHA1.

## Dependencies

- Do not add new dependencies without checking for known vulnerabilities (`pnpm audit`).
- Pin dependency versions in production; use lockfiles.
- Prefer well-maintained packages with active security patching.

## HTTP & API Security

- Always use HTTPS; never serve sensitive data over HTTP.
- Set security headers: `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`.
- Implement rate limiting on all public endpoints.
- CORS: use an allowlist, never `*` for credentialed requests.

## Data & Privacy

- Do not store PII beyond what is necessary.
- Anonymise or pseudonymise data used in non-production environments.
- Implement data retention policies — delete data when no longer needed.

## Reporting Vulnerabilities

If you identify a potential security issue during a task, **flag it immediately** even if it is outside the scope of the current task. Use this format:

```
⚠️ SECURITY: [brief title]
Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low
Location: [file:line]
Issue: [description]
Recommended fix: [suggestion]
```
